newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices ease ahead of cooler holiday.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices ease ahead of cooler holiday.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mostly softer Wednesday as forecasts called for the arrival of cooler weather in the East and Midwest over the long holiday weekend, industry sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted two to three cents lower around $2.13 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub.

"There's just nothing out there to support it. It will probably soften even more tomorrow," one trader said, citing the upcoming long holiday weekend, cooler forecasts and ample storage supplies as the main bearish culprits.

American Gas Association's storage data will be released later today, and most traders are expecting a build of 85-95 bcf to appear, according to a Reuter poll. This is compared with a gain of 93 bcf a year ago.
"If it's over 90 (bcf), this thing is going to crater," one trader said.
Meanwhile in the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate also softened a few cents to the high-$2.30s to low-$2.40s.
Continued heat in the Southwest was outweighed by an anticipated sharp drop in demand over the Independence Day holiday weekend, traders said.
As a result, Permian prices slipped three cents to about $2.00-2.01, while southern California border prices eased two cents to about $2.16-2.17.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit remained off line and was expected to return to service within the next two weeks.
In the Midwest, swing prices fell two cents to an average of $2.02, with Chicago city-gate talked around $2.15.
